Wait, `S(=O)(=O)C1` means the sulfur is part of the ring? No, `S(=O)(=O)` is a sulfonyl group attached to the ring carbon `C1`. Wait, `N(...)` and `S(=O)(=O)C1` are connected via `C1`. So it's a 6-membered ring containing N and S? Let's count: N-C-C-S-C-C? Actually, `N(c2...)c2...S(=O)(=O)C1` implies N is connected to C1, and S is connected to C1.
